'''Madaga-Ru''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Voss Mystics|Voss Mystic]] living during the [[Galactic War]].

==Biography==
Madaga-Ru was in some form a radical and a heretic among the other Mystics; he believed that his fellow [[Voss (species)|Voss]] lived in denial and only "[[Force vision/Legends|seeing]]" what they want to see. Madaga-Ru exiled himself and lived as a hermit in the dangerous wilds outside the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Voss-Ka]].<ref name="TOR" />

Around [[3640 BBY]] Madaga-Ru was approached by the [[Empire's Wrath]] in his search for the true [[Emperor's Voice (Sith Empire)|Voice of the Emperor]]. He explained to the Wrath that the Voice went missing in the [[Nightmare Lands]], where all who ventured were driven mad. He advised the Wrath to gain the [[Blessing of Oneness]] from a Mystic [[Vana-Xo]]<ref name="Request An Audience">{{TORcite|type=class|[[Empire's Wrath|Sith Warrior]]|Request An Audience|[[Voss]]}}</ref> and the [[Pendant of Bone]] from a [[Voss commandos|Voss commando]] [[Biddeck-Va]] to enter the [[Dark Heart]]. After the Wrath had acquired both objects, Madaga-Ru appeared before the Sith Warrior as a ghostly apparition, insisting on possessing the Wrath briefly as compensation for his assistance, regardless of consent.<ref name="Pendant of Bone">{{TORcite|type=class|[[Empire's Wrath|Sith Warrior]]|Pendant of Bone|[[Voss]]}}</ref>

After the Wrath had freed the Voice, Madaga-Ru appeared before the Sith warrior as an apparition, revealing that he gained the knowledge needed to keep [[Sel-Makor]] from escaping his prison, as well as warning that one person among the Wrath's crew was a traitor, but was unable to say their name. The traitor was later revealed to be [[Malavai Quinn]].

==Personality and traits==
Madaga-Ru admitted to preferring his hermit's way of life over the false pretenses of his people's civilization. Despite this disapproval of his culture, Madaga-Ru remained a true believer in the fundamental Voss way of life&mdash;a way of balance, simplicity and faith in the visions of the Mystics. Those who refused to respect Mystic philosophy or deliberately broke Voss law received Madaga-Ru's stern admonishment.
